claim_one_line: L133 -- OUTCOME NO-GO (simply connected form) against a criterion sealed and pushed (4c3c4775) BEFORE any cell ran, with the prior disclosed as NO-GO and FOUND named as the convenient answer needing the higher bar; IT DID NOT CLEAR IT. BANKED-IDENTITY GATE PASSED: dim Z(su(3)_colour) in e6 = 16 reproduced on the same instrument. (2) INNER INVOLUTIONS CANNOT REDUCE RANK, form-independently: all 63 sign-gradings of the E6 root system were built and EVERY ONE FIXES THE FULL CARTAN, so every inner-involution fixed subalgebra has rank 6. (3) THE OUTER ROUTE REACHES RANK 4 AND KILLS THE 27 DOING IT: E6's Dynkin diagram has EXACTLY ONE nontrivial automorphism tau, of order 2, swapping node pairs (0,5) and (2,4) -- computed here from the Cartan matrix -- and those are the nodes carrying the 27 and the 27-bar, so TAU EXCHANGES THE TWO AND ON Fix(tau) THEY BECOME ISOMORPHIC: THE 27 RESTRICTS SELF-DUAL. Self-duality is inherited by restriction to ANY subalgebra, so the entire outer route -- F4, C4 = sp(8), and every subalgebra of either -- makes the 27 REAL. This closes both rank-4 outer targets AT ONCE with one argument, is form-independent, and generalises B953/B954 from theta alone to the whole outer class. (4) THE SURVIVING HATCH IS TOO SMALL: B955 left exactly one hatch, the non-abelian images pi_1(m004) actually has, and measured here they give max elementary-abelian 2-rank A4 = 2, D5 = 1, S5 = 2 and 3-rank A4 = 1, D5 = 0, S5 = 1 -- NONE EXCEEDS RANK 2. By Steinberg's theorem (centralizers of semisimple elements in a SIMPLY CONNECTED group are connected): for commuting involutions x,y, Z(x) is connected, x lies in its centre hence in every maximal torus of Z(x), and y semisimple in Z(x) lies in some maximal torus T, so <x,y> is TORAL, its centralizer contains a torus, and the rank is 6. So ALL THREE of the object's available images give rank-6 centralizers, closing the hatch on both the 2- and 3-primary sides. (5) THE ONE HATCH THIS DOES NOT CLOSE, STATED PLAINLY: the torality step ASSUMES THE SIMPLY CONNECTED FORM; it breaks at rank 3 because Z(x) need not be simply connected (which is why E8 has its famous non-toral 2^5), and in the ADJOINT form E6/Z3 a RANK-2 elementary abelian subgroup CAN be non-toral. So the no-go is proved for the simply connected form, and if the object's representations land in the adjoint form a non-toral rank-2 subgroup is NOT excluded by this argument -- registered as L136. Note sections 2 and 3 are form-INDEPENDENT, so even in the adjoint case the outer route and single inner involutions stay closed; only the rank-2 non-toral inner case survives. (6) WHAT IT MEANS, combined with the banked chain -- measurement preserves rank (B952), theta reduces rank but deletes chirality (B954), abelian holonomy preserves rank necessarily (B955), and now every remaining centralizer route either preserves rank or makes the 27 real: THE OBJECT CANNOT REACH CHIRAL MATTER AT RANK 4 BY ANY CENTRALIZER CONSTRUCTION. This upgrades B952's 'closed by absence' toward CLOSED BY PROOF, with the adjoint-form hatch the honest remaining gap. It does NOT say the object cannot reach the SM -- B955 established that E6 -> SU(5) via two 27 VEVs does exactly that and is standard -- WHAT IS EXCLUDED IS THE CLASS OF OPERATIONS THE OBJECT ACTUALLY HAS; a Higgs-type mechanism remains unexcluded and remains unsupplied. LIMITS: the torality step is CITED not re-derived (Steinberg) and is the load-bearing citation; section 5's hatch is real, so this is a no-go for the simply connected form only; the 27's self-duality on Fix(tau) rests on the computed diagram swap plus the standard duality fact, the same statement as banked B582; and nothing here refutes FMT/SMT, B582 or B955, all of which stand.
